Keywords: Prussian local dues and religious pressure
RagShortTexts: Prussian communities differ in responses to rule and dues.
Leaders, households and clergy need not share one position.

Variants.Content: Prussian communities respond differently to demands over rule, dues and religion. Some seek patrons, retain customs or prepare resistance. Kin, livelihood and nearby posts affect choices; households judge burdens and protection beyond a leader’s consent.
A commander identifies actual Prussian participants and home guards. One chief’s promise does not levy a whole district; exhausted food and herds weaken later assembly.
Combining tribute, baptism and service indiscriminately can unite otherwise divided grievances. Separate terms identify partners able to keep cooperating.
Families fear demands and fields becoming battlegrounds. Relatives may disagree; seed stores and reliable news matter more than the loudest claim.
